This morning Alejandro asked me what happiness means to me.

And I got deep:

Real happiness isn’t things.
It’s a table full of family and friends,
loud conversations, shared traditions,
faith that grounds us,
and memories that outlive the night.

And you know what? That kind of happiness isn’t found it’s BUILT.
In choosing people over possessions.
In gratitude instead of comparison.
In growth over perfection.

Good lives aren’t perfect lives.
They are connected, intentional, kind.
They laugh often, love deeply,
and keep learning …. even when it’s hard.

Wishing you all of that and more - Feliz Navidad!😘🎄🎅🏼

If you believed Santa was real… 🎅
you already proved your brain is capable of creating belief first and evidence later.

Think about it.
You believed so fully that gifts appeared under the tree.
You didn’t “hope.”
You expected.

That’s not magic.
That’s conditioning.

Your brain didn’t need proof in advance.
It trusted the story it was given and organized your emotions, anticipation, and behavior around it.

And here’s the part no one tells you:
That same mechanism is still running your life today.

If your nervous system is conditioned to expect stress, disappointment, or “maybe someday,”
that’s exactly what it keeps recreating.

But when you re-train your subconscious to expect support, ease, and follow-through?
Your actions, decisions, and energy quietly start aligning to meet that expectation.

No woo.
No pretending.
Just neuroscience, nervous system regulation, and repetition.

You don’t need to “believe harder.”
You need to recondition the story your body is already living by.

Then…
🍴Choucroute Garnie
smoked pork & boudin blanc sausages, pork loin, smoked pork belly, Riesling-braised sauerkraut, juniper berries, steamed potatoes, Dijon mustard
🍴Baeckeoffe
traditional Alsatian casserole of lamb, oxtail, smoked pork belly, potatoes, braised in Pinot Gris with onions and thyme

To end, we shared the…
🍴Thin Caramelized Apple Tart

I finally went and here’s what you should know.
Would I recommend it if you’re short on time or visiting NYC for the first time? Honestly… maybe not.
 But if you love Christmas lights, local traditions, and something different from Midtown chaos, Dyker Heights is a fun detour.

Good to know before you go: • Dress warm, as everything is outdoors • please be mindful that it’s a residential area • During the weekends they have hot chocolate and snacks for sale • Guided tours are available, or take the R train to Bay Ridge

Crowds can get intense, so weeknights are the best time to visit if you’re looking for a more relaxed experience.

With love, care, and pure intention, we continue to create positive impact within our communities — and our Purple Christmas Celebration is a true reflection of that mission.

Purple Christmas started because our founder once experienced the holidays while living in a domestic violence shelter and understood firsthand how heavy that season can feel for survivors and their children. What began as a way to bring warmth, dignity, and joy into shelter spaces has grown into a tradition rooted in community, healing, and hope. This event is deeply personal to us, and it represents everything Sisters In Purple stands for: showing up, loving loudly, and making sure families know they are not alone.

This was more than a toy drive — this is what it looks like when a community comes together with the right intentions. From laughter and smiles to moments of genuine connection, our children left feeling like they were surrounded by family that truly loves and cares about them. ☕🎨🎄

Today I wanted to share a different take on pick playing. 
On Beatles “I Saw Her Standing There” Paul McCartney is using his classic Hofner Bass with a pick. He is playing closer to the neck to make this warmer tone that we hear. I chose to play more in the middle on the bass, because I was having a very hard time on playing this line clean at this tempo at the neck. I find it harder to control the bass there with a pick, and it really goes to show how great a bassist he is! He’s take is quite clean!

caption:
My most recent stay in NYC saw me being guested by a childhood friend who lives in the old stomping grounds of Harlem, east through west, that I grew up in.

Though an attempt at gentrification — that seems to have stalled a bit — is detectable with the default introductions of homogenous staples such as Starbucks, Trader Joe’s, Whole Foods, et al, there are still homegrown, non-chain businesses that that have taken root and are starting to shine.

One of those places I discovered was directly across the street where I was Staying. It’s called @azarakitchen, and is the brainchild of Ousmane Compaore, chef and restauranteur from Burkina Faso.

The menu is touted as “African and Mediterranean” and boasts respectful representations of traditional dishes — expertly prepared and and impressively delicious — from those widespread and varied provenances.

In two nearly back-to-back visits, I was treated to a *maffe lamb* dinner dish of long-cooked on-the-bone lamb in an aromatically flavored peanut and vegetable broth, and followed that up with a booze-free version of tiramisu that finally offers my a more than rewarding opportunity to enjoy my second favorite dessert (after banana pudding) without the feel of sacrifice in taste or texture.

My second visit I was curious to to see how the globally ubiquitous chicken wings could stand out from the countless number of other iterations, and Azara’s “spicy sticky” wings are uniquely seasoned and properly stand out from common wing editions by transporting the palate to places more exotic and authentic to the regions these globally individual flavor profiles get their inspirations from.

If I were still in the neighborhood, and possibly not even, Azara Kitchen, I would be a frequent visitor for not only the food and the obvious love that it comes from, but for the charming vibe and layout, accentuated by some well thought out wall art and an attentively pleasant staff. 

Gentrification or not, Azara Kitchen should be a neighborhood standout that should continue being a rightful success for locals and visitors for a great many years.

- Shrimps & Grits 
- Ginger Juice 🫚 

Thoughts?💭 
Zac visited nyc again and when asked what he wanted to eat, he half joking half not said African food. We both like trying new food so decided to go with west african for lunch. 

The jollof rice with lamb tasted good flavor wise, but it had a greater portion of rice than stew w/lamb. The lamb was cooked well, but pretty chewy and more bone than meat. Zac thought his shrimp and grits was well seasoned and I thought it was soo creamy and delicious 🤤 They have homemade drinks in 4 different flavors and we got the ginger drink. Apparently, you could get it hot or cold so we did half hot/half cold to try both. We both preferred the hot version, but it’s really spicy so hits the back of your throat. It felt great for chilly weather and soothed my sore throat. Server was friendly and gave us good recommendations! 

I’d want to try more west African staples like fufu next time, but all these restaurants are in Harlem or the Bronx 😭

Just like that, I’m back from my summer in New York City as an intern with @nbcnews. I still feel like the luckiest girl in the world that I got to work this dream internship, and the actual experience turned out better than I ever could have imagined. 

There is SO much to reflect on, starting with the fact that I am so grateful to have had this exposure to national news. The Specials Unit had no shortage of work this summer, and I’m honored to have played a role in covering our country’s biggest breaking stories.

The job went from adrenaline jolts to long-form work, keeping my days exciting and versatile. The best part was that my team truly taught and challenged me enough to contribute significant work. Here are some of the stories we covered: 

- The birthright citizenship and gender affirming care SCOTUS decisions
- The Israel/Iran conflict and US involvement
- ICE protests in LA and across the nation
- The verdicts of Sean “Diddy” Combs and Karen Read
- The sentencing of University of Idaho murderer Bryan Kohberger
- The central Texas floods
- The shooting at the Fort Stewart Army Base
- Consistent coverage of President Trump taking questions from reporters

I remember the tasks looking so daunting on that first day, wondering if I could seriously learn it all in just 10 weeks. All the thanks goes to the incredible team of journalists that guided me through with so much patience. I now feel significantly more confident in my production and editorial decision-making skills (and, shocker, 10x more in love with journalism). 

My last day in the newsroom had a total “last day of school” feel to it- the energy was high, we had lunch as a team and it was perfectly sunny outside. We even had some unexpected breaking news, giving us interns the chance to culminate everything we learned one last time in person together. The day ended later because of it, but it felt like it went by in 5 seconds- as did the entire summer. 

I am walking out of this filled with gratitude and so much love for what (I think) is the coolest job in the world. Thank you NBC News and NYC for the summer of my dreams ❤️

I found out I had won when @marcmaron (!) announced it on “Short Attention Span Theater.” It included airfare, hotel (The Royalton, a super hip boutique hotel that had been recently opened by Studio 54 vet Ian Schrager), the Here and Now taping, and tickets to @nbcsnl on 11/21/1992 (host @sinbadbad musical guest @sade ). The first night, we had some nice folks from Comedy Central pick us up, take us to a nice dinner and then to the taping. After it dragged on, they leaned in and asked, “Do you want to get out of here?” We did, so the car picked us up and took us to Elaine’s for a comedy set by Ellen DeGenerous.
 
The next day, a different couple from the channel picked us up. They were younger and seemed like more “junior rank” folks. No matter, we started by dining at a fabulous seafood restaurant with amazing Picasso plates adorning the walls. Upon arriving at 30 Rock, we went to will call to get our tickets but they didn’t have any for us. The Comedy Central folks looked panicked and mortified. Fortunately, I had reached out to band leader @gesmithmusic through Liberty Records (he and the band had an album out on the label at the time). I mentioned that the label had arranged for me meet G.E. before the show and the door person said something to the effect of, “Well, why didn’t you say so!” They escorted all four of us to the stage and, sure enough, G.E. came out and was an extremely gracious host. He showed me his amp setup and a few of his vintage guitars. As it was approaching show time, G.E. excused himself and the door person said we could sit anywhere we liked except for the swivel chairs at the front of the stage. @thedanacarvey and Phil Hartman opened the show, impersonating George Bush and Bill Clinton. It was post-election and Clinton had just won. Dana as Bush broke down weeping, saying, “I’m a Jimmy Carter!,” in reference to his one-and-done term. Sade was fabulous, of course, and Polly and I enjoyed a very memorable weekend

In my head, I have such an affinity towards @americanbarnyc and honestly… these days I’m unsure why 

Don’t get me wrong, it’s definitely good, and I enjoy a split salad and cheeseburger combo. But something was weird and very different than the American bar I’ve been to over the last 5 years. It didn’t feel as pristine as it once was, I had to swat away a fly once or twice, and we really didn’t receive any service at all.

We were able to snag a table for 6 at 2 pm day of on a Saturday, so for that I am thankful.. but I’d rather go with a smaller group and sit at the bar for the elevated experience you’re ultimately paying for

Heres what we got:
- cheeseburger ⭐️⭐️⭐️ this was very delicious, I believe smaller than it once was though. The pickle chips are always a great addition.The fries were crispy and very salty, I looove ketchup and mayo as a side.
- chopped salad ⭐️⭐️ I used to dream of this salad it was so good, cucumber, tomato, chickpea, soppressata, queso fresco and house vinaigrette, I even used to recreate this at home!! For me, I love when a salad has WAY more toppings than lettuce…which is one of the reasons I loved this. As you can see, they changed the entire topping / lettuce ratio. The big, dense $30 salads they were once known for are now same price, same size, way more lettuce🙄🥴
- peanut chicken salad - didn’t try this, but received feedback that it was enjoyable. Brussels sprouts, avocado, carrots, sesame sticks, radish, peanut dressing and chicken 👍🏻

Now for the service… we didn’t see our waiter more than 2-3 times for a fairly long sit. Did not warn us kitchen closed at 3, didn’t come around to ask if we wanted anything other than 1 drink and our meal. I understand there’s only so much a waiter can do, and there was a 20 minute period where the restaurant was pretty busy, but we were truly left unattended which reduces points from the experience. Especially when they walked past us 10x times with not even a glance when we tried to get their attention

I recommend the first come first serve bar. The martinis are always very good, especially now that I’m an “in and out” ordered on the vermouth. 🥳🍸🍸🍸🍔🍟

Why These Pink Dolphins Look Unreal — And Why They’re Disappearing

This 12-second clip shows Amazon river dolphins, also called pink botos, surfacing playfully in calm freshwater 🌊🐬

Their pink color isn’t artificial or rare genetics — it comes from blood vessels close to the skin, which become more visible as they age, get excited, or gain scars from play and competition.

Despite viral claims, these dolphins aren’t the “rarest in the world.” Experts estimate around 100,000 still live across the Amazon basin. However, conservation groups warn their numbers are falling fast. The IUCN lists them as endangered, with populations declining by up to 50% in some regions due to dams, pollution, fishing nets, and habitat loss.

Unlike extremely rare leucistic ocean dolphins, pink botos are naturally colored and deeply tied to Amazonian culture. Indigenous folklore even describes them as shape-shifters who transform into humans at night — a reminder of how science and storytelling often coexist in nature.

Beautiful, intelligent, and vulnerable — these dolphins are a symbol of why freshwater ecosystems matter more than we think.

🌟 Why Choose a Primary Care Physician Over Urgent Care?

Your health deserves more than quick fixes. While urgent care is great for sudden needs, a PCP like Dr. Cathleen Saros offers something urgent care can’t:

✅ Continuity of Care – Dr. Saros knows your history, your goals, and your story. That means smarter, more personalized treatment.

Bar Primi on 33rd, next to Moynihan Train Station, gets as much right as it does wrong. But what it does get right is absolutely extraordinary. First and foremost- the setting. 5 out of 5 stars. The outdoor walk up space is luxe and offers adequate heating options for a chillier day. The indoor dining is immaculate from art to color scheme. 

The food? Outstanding, and an outstanding value. The three course pre fixe is perfectly priced, very generously portioned, and offers a good variety of what is available on the standard menu. Except very poorly plated  Where it looked pretty, it was hard to eat. The brussels were overabundant in a small dish, making spilling impossible to avoid. And dessert was similarly hard to navigate. 

Now where Bar Primi fumbled - service. My app was served promptly but my entree took well over half an hour, despite my saying off the bat I was on my lunch hour. When I found myself with just 15 minutes to spare to eat both entree and dessert ? I requested my entree boxed and my dessert and check given to me at the same time. Somehow my server struggled to grasp this ask and I had to repeat myself five times over. And even then there was a five minute gap between dessert and bill. I’ve worked food service before, I know there’s a lot to juggle. But the place had two other tables dining beside me and it was 2pm on a Tuesday. The cherry atop this? While I waited I had to hear a loud conversation the hostess and my server held where the hostess vehemently complained about a prior customer and her coworkers. A really, really unprofessional thing to do on the floor. 

My advice? Come during dinner when they hopefully aren’t staffed by their B squad. Or check out another of their locations. Or enjoy the outdoor space and don’t dine when you’re pressed for time. Because, again, the food itself was absolutely phenomenal.

Dear Valued Guests,

After nearly 10 wonderful years of serving our community, we regret to share that Tuscany Steakhouse will be closing its doors, with our final day of service being Wednesday, December 31, 2025.

This decision was not made lightly. Unfortunately, due to a significant and unexpected increase in rent, continuing operations is no longer financially sustainable. We sincerely apologize for the short notice and understand this news may come as a disappointment. Please know that this was not how we ever envisioned this chapter ending.

We are incredibly grateful for your loyalty, support, and friendships over the years. Tuscany Steakhouse has been more than a restaurant — it has been a family, and that is because of you.

We would be honored to welcome you one last time. Please join us before December 31 for a final meal, a toast, and a proper farewell.

And while this chapter is coming to a close, our family continues. Please don’t forget our sister restaurant, Il Monello, where we would be honored to continue serving you.
